chapter_title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths

12.original: [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning]
12.content: which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Three Great States and the Two Spiritual Deaths

---

**¶1:** There exist three great and mighty spiritual states in all; and also two great and bitter forms of spiritual death.

**¶2:** What are these three great states? Or again, what are these two forms of death that are bitter?

**¶4:** The first state is the celestial principle itself, the Divine Human. From the time when the celestial principle descended into the deepest conditions of falsity from evil and was overwhelmed by them; and the Divine Truth proceeding from the Divine Love was sent forth, which went down and drew that principle upward. After the celestial principle had been elevated, the Divine Love and the Divine Wisdom established all things in order — the interiors and the exteriors of the whole spiritual world.

**¶5:** Furthermore, the Divine Rational manifested and took its dwelling in the doctrinal vessel of that illuminated state. It displayed the fullness of the Divine likeness, and it separated wisdom from all its admixture with falsity throughout every created thing. It proceeded through the highest celestial degrees. Until the time when the old state of the church is dissolved, all its falsities laid bare, the final love of judgment released, and the completed form of the regenerated Grand Man ascends into fullness. These three great workings were begun in this first state, when the celestial principle was sent forth with its five faculties of spiritual perception into confrontation with evil.

**¶6:** In contrast, [GAP-1: the first spiritual death] is the condition in which falsity from evil commingled with the five perceptive faculties of the celestial principle.

**¶7:** The second state is the time when those who dwell in wisdom, who were victorious in the combats of temptation, will be established upon their states of governance in the regenerated spiritual world and will dwell in the renewed external of the mind. And they reign in the regenerated life until the Divine itself unveils its own likeness above them.

**¶8:** The measure of the sojourn in the regenerated state is equal to the measure of the first state passed in spiritual affliction and temptation. They will reign in this manner and experience blessedness in the regenerated life.

**¶9:** The great third state [GAP-2: is the time] when the Divine itself will unveil over them its own likeness [GAP-3: in fullness beyond comprehension] and raises them up [GAP-4: into itself] and receives them into the inmost hidden treasury of the Divine memory [GAP-5: where nothing of falsity can enter] and gives [GAP-6: to each one the fullness of] its own life. The Divine can pour out upon them [GAP-7: without measure] its celestial delight and its sweet perception of good, which removes all suffering that they have known through their understanding. [GAP-8: There is] fullness and an eternal joy! When the Divine grace would satiate them completely, it gives to them its [GAP-9: own likeness renewed] and they are made new within those gifts.

**¶10:** Also, the Divine can gather them once more into peace and interior silence, and bring their spiritual form to the same fullness of stature as the first celestial degrees. And it establishes each faculty in its proper degree, in its own state of life. They will dwell in the regenerated life, each within their proper degrees!

**¶11:** Now, when they dwell in their proper degrees, they will become rich in wisdom and good beyond all measure, eternally, beyond any succession of states. From then on they will not reckon any passage of time among them, nor the number of the states, nor the changes, from generation to generation, eternally. The Divine will not be hidden from them from this time onward. Rather, it has accomplished its full unveiling to them [GAP-10: in perpetuity] — the Divine being revealed to them forever.

**¶12:** These are the three great spiritual states, [GAP-11: to which the Divine itself has assigned their order in the providence of all things].

**¶13:** In contrast, the two spiritual deaths are these.

**¶14:** The first spiritual death extends from the time when wisdom fell into falsity and was commingled with the ruling evils of the hells, until the time when wisdom will become pure and will be separated from falsity in the final love of judgment. Whatever remains behind of the good, however fragmented, can build up and add to the completed form of the Grand Man — the Last Statue of regenerated humanity.

**¶15:** Now, the second spiritual death is the death in which the interiors of those who lived from evil will perish — when [GAP-12: they will] be stripped of the shining truth that illuminates the understanding. And also they are separated from the living influx of heaven, from which they received [GAP-13: living] spiritual respiration; and they are deprived of the living good itself, which [GAP-14: sustained all things] in the world; and they are severed and swept away from the completed Grand Man [GAP-15: having no part in it] and bound upon [GAP-16: the falsity from their own evil] — the will turned inward upon itself will become [GAP-17: the very source of] their torment and their affliction; for their works [GAP-18: have consigned them to] those three infernal regions; because they have profaned and rejected the Divine proceeding through every successive state of the church.

**¶16:** These are the two spiritual deaths. The first spiritual death is temporal — it has a boundary, and ends when purification is complete; [GAP-19: but] the second spiritual death is eternal. It is the second death!

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: There exist three great mighty days in all; and also two great and bitter deaths.
What are these three great days? Or again, what are these two deaths that are bitter?

The first day is our father, the Man. From the time when the First Man went down to the abyss of darkness and drowned in it; and the Living Spirit was sent, who went and bore him up. After the Man had ascended, the Father of Life and the Great Spirit set things in order, and the worlds above and below.

Furthermore, the glorious Ambassador came and dwelt in the ship of the day. He displayed his glorious image, and he purified the light out of all things. He walked in the heights of the heavens. Till the time when the world will be dissolved, all things destroyed, the great fire released, and the Last Statue ascends. These three deeds were begun on this first day, when they sent the First Man with his five sons.
In contrast, [the first death] is the darkness that mixed with the five sons of the First Man.

The second day is the time when the fathers of light, who were victorious in the struggle, will sit on their thrones in the new aeon and dwell on the new earth. And they reign in the new aeon till the Father unveils his image above them.
The length of the sojourn in the new aeon equals the measure of the first day spent in affliction. They will reign like this and rejoice in the new aeon.

The great third day [is the time] when the Father will unveil over them his image [ ... ... ] and he raises them up [to himself] and he receives them into his hidden treasury [of light] and he gives [to them] his soul. He can pour out upon them [without measure] his ambrosia and his sweet perfume, which takes away all affliction that they have seen with their eyes. [It is a] fullness and a joy eternal! When his grace would sate them, he gives to them his [garments of light] and they are made anew in them.

Also, he can summon them once more in peace and silence, and perfect their stature in same measure as his first aeons. And he sets each power in its aeon, in its dwelling-place. They will dwell in the new aeon in their aeons!

Now, when they dwell in their aeons, they will become rich beyond measure, for ever, beyond time. From then on they will not count that season amongst them; nor the number of the days, nor the hours, generation after generation, for ever and ever. The Father will not be hidden from them, from this time on. Rather, he has accomplished (his) unveiling to them [for ever] he being revealed to them for ever.
These are the three great days, [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning].
In contrast, the two deaths are these.

The first death is from the time when the light fell to the darkness, and was mixed in with the rulers of Darkness; until the time when the light will become pure, and be separated from the darkness in that great fire. The remainder left behind there can build and add to that Last Statue.

Now, the second death is the death in which the souls of sinful men shall die; when [they will] be stripped of the shining light that illuminates the world. And also they are separated from the living air, from which they receive [living] breath; and they are deprived of this living soul, which [sustains all things] in the world; and they are separated and swept away from this Last Statue [and they have no portion in it] and bound on [ ... ... ] the female will become [the source of] their torture and their affliction; for their deeds [have cast them into] those three places; because they have blasphemed and despised the Holy Spirit since [ev]ery generation of the world.
These are the two deaths. The first death is temporal; [but] the second death is eternal. It is the sec[ond deat]h!

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms "the first spiritual death," and the text's structure in ¶13–14 explicitly names "the first death" in parallel, making the editor's reconstruction correct.
The formula "is the time when" directly parallels ¶7's "The second day is the time when," and the spiritual reading confirms this phrasing.
The spiritual reading says "into itself," meaning the Divine raises the redeemed into union with itself; in the Kephalaia's natural register this is "to himself," referring to the Father.
The "treasury of light" is a standard Manichaean technical term for the inmost divine realm where nothing of darkness can enter, matching the spiritual reading's "where nothing of falsity can enter."
The spiritual reading says "to each one the fullness of"; in the Kephalaia's concise clause-pattern ("and he gives … his soul"), the natural dative complement is "to them."
The spiritual reading says "without measure," and the text itself uses the phrase "beyond measure" in ¶11, showing this expression belongs to the text's own vocabulary for divine superabundance.

The spiritual reading indicates a declarative "There is," and the exclamatory sentence structure ("fullness and a joy eternal!") requires an introductory copular phrase; "It is a" declares that the unveiled state is itself fullness and joy.

The spiritual reading says "own likeness renewed"; in Manichaean soteriology the divine likeness restored to the redeemed is the "garments of light," and the plural form explains the subsequent pronoun "in them."

The spiritual reading says "in perpetuity," and the Kephalaia's own register for eternal permanence is "for ever," which also creates the emphatic doubling typical of the text ("for ever … for ever").

fills.explanation: The editor's reconstruction uses standard Kephalaia terminology — "Father of Greatness" for the supreme deity and "given number to in the reckoning" for divine ordering — matching the spiritual reading's "assigned their order in the providence of all things."
The spiritual reading confirms "they will," and the grammar requires a subject and future auxiliary before "be stripped."
The spiritual reading confirms "living," and the text's own pattern repeats "living" as a qualifier throughout (living air, living soul), making "living breath" the natural parallel.
The spiritual reading says "sustained all things"; the Living Soul in Manichaean cosmology is the divine light scattered throughout creation that sustains and vivifies all things in the world.

fills.fill: and they have no portion in it
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "having no part in it"; being swept away from the Last Statue means exclusion from the final redeemed form, and "no portion in it" is standard Kephalaia language for eschatological exclusion.

The spiritual reading says "the very source of"; the female (Âz/concupiscence) becomes the origin and cause of their torment, and "the source of" captures this causal relationship in the Kephalaia's register.

The spiritual reading says "have consigned them to"; in the Kephalaia's vivid eschatological register, deeds actively "cast" sinners into their punitive regions, connecting evil works to their infernal consequences.
The spiritual reading confirms "but" as the contrastive conjunction between the temporal first death and the eternal second death, and the adversative structure is required by the text's logic.
